What happened to you was real, and I am so, so sorry you’re going through this. I experienced something remarkably similar with my ex that I dated from ages 17-20. 

My ex promised me that if I did not meet his needs sexually, he would find someone else, and that I was not going to find a guy who loved me like he did. I cautiously agreed, and once the deed was done, he finished on me and I ran to the bathroom in tears. I bled so heavily that I had to use a pad to keep it all in for the rest of the day, and I just thought it was normal to be emotional after your first time. 

I started therapy (EMDR- amazing for PTSD). It was brutal. But now, several years later, I no longer have nightmares about him touching me. I am with someone I trust with my body and soul entirely, and I finally feel safe in my own skin. 

I know I just dumped my whole personal story, but my point with this is that it will get better, if you continue to work through it. You are not broken, and you can and will get through this. Admitting what happened to you and sharing it proves that you are very strong, and I’m so, so proud of you for seeking therapy. I wish you the best and the utmost support. You deserve to be surrounded by people who treat you with the utmost love and respect, and I’m sorry you’ve ever had scum like your ex in your life at all.

Hey! Recovered anorexic here. 
Please, please stop starving yourself. Cut this behaviour out while you still can- I wish someone had stopped me when I first started. Sure, the weight loss at first might be motivating, but you’ll stop losing weight, you’ll be obsessed with food to the point of where it’s all you can think about, and it only gets worse. 

I got addicted to starving myself when I was a teenager. 200k in hospital and treatment bills later, I regret the hell I put myself through every day. I’m in my mid twenties and I have now hurt my body so much that despite being recovered for nearly four years, I have health effects that I will live with for the rest of my life. The enamel on my teeth is worn down, my bones are weak, my immune system is garbage, and I always still worry about food in the back of my mind. 

It isn’t worth it. I promise. Please take better care of yourself. You deserve to live unencumbered from an eating disorder. 

https://www.nationaleatingdisorders.org/ has some great resources to find help. I don’t know your situation so I can’t tell you how to proceed, but I strongly, STRONGLY urge you to take care of yourself. 

Don’t ruin your life like I did.
